memos.risk:
Risk officer assessment for OnionWeb (ORGANIC class, alive, age 30.5 min, pool ~157 SOL):

Sizing: Pool depth is adequate but the coin is hot. Last 15 min volume ~$142k with net flow only +53 SOL against $554 SOL sold, and sellers (878) nearly match buyers (1075). Early buy pressure was dominated by a launch bot and a 63% bundle share, so a ticket of $5 is the sane maximum; $10-$20 is not justified given fee drag of 1.4-5.1%.

Stop: 25% from entry, tight, since it is already 18% off its 30-min high and momentum is fading.

Hold: 15-30 min. The coin is past the typical window; a bounce is possible but base rates say most coins don't recover dips.

Refuse entirely if: the bundle/launch-bot concentration is confirmed as coordinated, or drawdown exceeds ~25% before our order lands. Given the sell-heavy flow, my recommendation is to skip unless the desk has a specific reason to take a $5 speculative position.
memos.scout: The case for buying is real but thin. Volume is substantial: $141.8k over the last 15 minutes with 1,075 buyers, and the coin is still up 81% in that window. The bundle share is high, at 63%, which is a warning sign, though 932 total buyers and a top-3 share of only 7% suggest the holder base is not concentrated. The first two minutes after graduation show 370 non-agent buyers, a top-5 buyer share of 13%, and a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.86, so early flow was not dominated by a few wallets. Net flow over the last 15 minutes was positive at +53 SOL. Against that, the coin is already 18% off its 30-minute high, 878 sellers are active in the same window, and the 63% bundle share means much of the apparent demand may be coordinated. Pool depth of 157 SOL is adequate for a $20 ticket, but the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost is material. I do not see a strong case that demand will hold for another 30-60 minutes. This is a marginal, skip-leaning setup.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a late-stage distribution after the 81% last-15-minute run. The bundled curve (63.5% bundle share, 1,075 buyers in 15 min) and the 0.86 sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation suggest early wallets are exiting into retail demand. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is only +52.98 SOL against 554 SOL sold, so most of the buying is being absorbed by sellers. The 17.8% drawdown from the 30-minute high has already started, and at a 157 SOL pool, a $20 ticket with a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost needs a sustained move just to break even. The creator-side completer share of 31% also points to insider exits. Skip.
